name: Regenerate & Relink – Thumbnails, Image URLs & Media Cleanup
author: Takashi Fujisaki

sections.description:
WordPress bakes image size file names into your post content the moment you insert an image. When a size definition changes later — a new theme, new media settings — regenerating thumbnails is not enough: the URLs in your content still point to the old files, leaving broken images or outdated dimensions. Unused thumbnails pile up and waste disk space.

Regenerate & Relink fixes the whole chain, safely:

  • Diagnose – list every registered image size with file counts, disk usage, how often it is used in content, and which files need regeneration.
  • Regenerate – rebuild intermediate sizes from the original images. Never from -scaled copies.
  • Relink – update image URLs, width / height attributes and [caption] widths in post content to match the current definitions. Only the file name part of the URL is touched — your CDN and site structure are preserved.
  • Clean up – quarantine files that are no longer referenced anywhere, instead of deleting them. Restore anytime; auto-purge after 30 days (configurable).
  • Dry-run first – every stage shows a full preview before touching anything. Skipped items are reported with reasons and links.
  • Replace, rename or move one image – from the attachment edit screen, replace an image with another one by drag and drop (a different format is fine), rename its files, or move them to another folder in uploads. Image URLs in your posts follow, old files that are no longer used go to the quarantine area, and the last operation can be undone in one step.
  • WP-CLI – scan, review reports and apply from the command line.

The plugin never changes your image size definitions. It detects what was changed elsewhere — Settings > Media, your theme's add_image_size() — and brings files and content back in sync.
sections.changelog:
0.3.0

  • New: Replace an image by drag and drop. On the attachment edit screen, drop the new image onto the image or the "Replace, rename or move" box, or into the "Replace image" window.
  • After you drop or choose an image, the preview of the affected posts opens right away. As before, nothing changes until you confirm.

0.2.1

  • The box on the attachment edit screen is now titled "Replace, rename or move". The Quarantine tab, its "Empty" confirmation and wp regenerate-relink restore also mention moving an image to another folder.

0.2.0

  • New: Replace an image with another one while keeping its attachment ID. A different format works too (for example JPEG to WebP); intermediate sizes are created with your current size settings.
  • New: Rename an image's files, move them to another folder in uploads, or both at once. The original, -scaled, all intermediate sizes and image-edit backups are handled together.
  • After a replace, rename or move, image URLs in post content follow automatically, old files that are no longer used go to the quarantine area, and "Undo last operation" restores the files, the attachment data and the post content.
  • The operations are available on the attachment edit screen and from the row actions in the Media Library list view.

0.1.3

  • Starting with the next update, Dashboard > Updates shows the plugin's icon, and the "View details" window shows its banner. The images are bundled with the plugin, so displaying them sends no request to GitHub.

0.1.2

  • Added a Settings link on the Plugins screen. It opens the Settings tab of Tools > Regenerate & Relink.

0.1.1

  • Added an update checker. New versions now appear on the Plugins screen and can be installed from there.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
